title: Mljet 2026: Car Rental vs Public Transport Facts
metaDescription: Deciding on transport in Mljet 2026? Compare car rental costs, public bus routes, and ferry connections. Get concrete facts for navigating Mljet National Park and beyond.
content:
## Car Rental: Essential for Discovery
A rental car offers full autonomy on Mljet. Daily rates for a compact vehicle average €40-€70 during the peak summer season (July/August 2026), dropping to €30-€50 off-peak. Agencies operate at Sobra, Polače, and Pomena ferry ports; pre-booking months ahead is critical, especially for summer. Fuel is available only at a single station near Goveđari. Expect parking fees, notably €5-€10/day within Mljet National Park, although many other spots are free. Renting a car on Mljet is an investment in time and convenience, not a luxury.

## Public Transport: Extremely Limited Reach
Mljet's public transport is sparse. A limited bus service primarily connects Sobra ferry port with Polače and Pomena, stopping near the Mljet National Park entrance (Vrata od Solina). Frequencies are low; even in peak summer, expect only 3-5 daily connections, significantly less in the shoulder seasons. Ticket prices are generally €3-€5 per ride, distance dependent. Accessing popular spots like Saplunara beach in the east, remote hiking trails, or other villages beyond the main route is nearly impossible without private transport. Most travelers overestimate the reliability of Mljet's public transport; it functions primarily as a ferry shuttle, not island-wide transport.

## Recommendation
For comprehensive exploration, a rental car is highly recommended. It unlocks hidden beaches, viewpoints, and provides flexibility to match ferry schedules without long waits. Public transport suits only those staying within walking distance of the National Park entrance and not venturing far.

faq.question: Is it possible to visit Mljet National Park without a car?
faq.answer: Yes, buses connect Sobra ferry port directly to the park entrance, and park ferries operate within the park's lakes.

faq.question: Are taxis available on Mljet?
faq.answer: Yes, taxis are available at ferry ports and main villages, but they are expensive for extensive island travel.

faq.question: How long does it take to drive across Mljet?
faq.answer: Driving from Sobra (east) to Pomena (west) takes approximately 45-60 minutes, covering the island's main length.

quickAnswer: Mljet's limited public transport makes a rental car almost essential for comprehensive island exploration, especially for accessing the National Park and various villages efficiently. While a bus connects the ferry port to the park entrance, a car provides freedom, saves time, and significantly enhances the travel experience.
